parent_pptx.core_properties_interpretation: Container/account metadata as stored in the PPTX; it does not establish human authorship or image-generation history.

source_context.note: Context attribution is separate from metadata. No creator identity, generation dates, prompts, model, ownership chain or missing history has been manufactured.

policies.originals: Byte-identical copies of the embedded PPTX media, including source metadata; no retouching, resizing or recompression.
policies.references: Full original pixel dimensions. WebP quality 90 by default; lossy encoding changes pixels and omits metadata.
policies.thumbnails: WebP quality 85 by default, maximum edge 480 pixels, proportional LANCZOS downsampling and no upscaling.
policies.comparison: Compare each reference.path to its linked original.path; dimensions, byte counts and SHA-256 hashes are recorded for both.
policies.c2pa: Limited JPEG APP11 marker detection only. No cryptographic signature, claim chain or assertion verification was performed. Original bytes retain the metadata; web derivatives do not carry its signature.

source_text_objects: "This isn't a textbook, and it sure as hell isn't a philosophy degree. Life doesn't hand you a pristine 500-page manual printed on glossy paper—it throws you into the deep end with a roll of duct tape and tells you to figure it out. This book is that roll of duct tape. No fluff, no academic jargon, no high-minded theory. Just the raw, functional, rough-as-guts rules for navigating everything from fixing a leaky tap to surviving human interaction, without losing your sanity."
"Look, most guides are written by experts who forgot what it's like to know absolutely nothing. They give you step 12 when you haven't even found the toolbox yet.

is built on a simple premise: if it works, it works. We’re stripping away the polish, skipping the filler, and getting straight to the dirt-under-the-fingernails basics of how things actually operate in the real world. Grab a drink, pull up a chair, and let's get into it."

"Perfection is a trap. If you wait until you have the perfect tools, the perfect plan, or the perfect understanding, you’ll spend your whole life standing on the sidelines. Welcome to the rough-as-guts approach to life: dirty solutions that actually work, survival skills for everyday chaos, and practical wisdom forged in trial and error. You don't need a diploma to master the universe—you just need enough grit to patch the holes as you go."
